texts: good. the record, the ending, day 720 and Year 2 are all carried and nothing is over-asserted. The one residue is that "day 720" lands in our calendar day-of-month slot, so it will not order against other dated events — a gap on our side that no rewrite of your sentence can close.

mixed: the reserve, the holding, day 720 and the past tense are all there, but "ten months of supply" has no bearer — the figure ends up measuring the holding event rather than the stock, so "how much did the reserve have?" does not bind to the reserve — and the parse also mints a standalone genus claim about "mire-essence" that your sentence never makes (it only ever names the compound "mire-essence reserve"). Naming the substance and stating the projection as a finite consequence fixes both: "On day 720, the mire-essence reserve held enough mire-essence to last ten months."

mixed: same shape as the mire-essence line — the eight-week figure measures the holding event rather than the store's stock, and a standalone genus claim about "salt-bloom" is minted although your sentence only names the compound "salt-bloom store". Rewrite as: "On day 720, the salt-bloom store held enough salt-bloom to last eight weeks."

mixed: the store, the holding, day 720 and the past tense are all carried and nothing extra is asserted here, but as with the other two stores "nine weeks of supply" leaves the figure measuring the holding event rather than the stock. Rewrite as: "On day 720, the feather store held enough feathers to last nine weeks."

bad: the hedge is lost. "Estimated fourteen sky-cats" comes out as a standing group of fourteen sky-cats asserted as fact, with the estimating merely sitting beside it, so a reasoner will treat fourteen as the true population rather than as the census's estimate. Put the count inside a that-clause so it is recorded as the content of the estimate: "On day 720, the sky-cat census estimated that there were fourteen sky-cats."

good. the count rides the group and the per-member rule is fireable, so any Keeper you name later inherits the day-720 active state. The one shortfall — a flat "was this Keeper active?" has to go through the reified state rather than a plain atom — is ours to fix in the translator, not yours.

bad: "returned to active station-tending" forces two improvisations — the abstract activity is filed under the spatial "goal" slot, as if she moved somewhere, and "station-tending" is unpacked with machinery meant for obligations and capabilities rather than for an ordinary referring phrase — so "what did she go back to doing?" lands on a shape nothing else in the corpus shares. Say it with finite clauses: "In the late spring of Year 2, Aelis Brae was active and tended stations again." ("Late spring" can still only be recorded as a bare label beside Year 2 — we have no season term — but that costs you nothing here.)
